title: m365-integration tests import @electric-sql/pglite, which NO workspace member declares - it is hoisted from originate's prisma, so a Prisma bump breaks two suites with a load failure
description:
## BLUF

**Two** `m365-integration` **test files import** `@electric-sql/pglite`**, and NO workspace member declares it.** It is present in `node_modules` only as a transitive dependency of **another service's** Prisma: `services/originate` → `prisma@7.8.0` → `@prisma/dev@0.24.3` → `@electric-sql/pglite@0.4.1`, hoisted to `Blockchain/Dev/node_modules/`. So two of this service's suites load today by accident of originate's dependency tree, and any Prisma change that drops or restructures `@prisma/dev` breaks them with a load failure.

**This is LATENT, not present.** A clean `npm ci` in a fresh clone of develop resolves it and the m365 suite runs green — measured, see below. Nothing is failing now.

## Measured at develop `108091b2e1c1c9d4b486213b6424ebfe88ef9332`

In a fresh clone, after `npm ci` (rc 0, 1937 packages) and `npm run build --workspace=packages/shared`:

| reading | result |
| -- | -- |
| `@electric-sql/pglite` in `services/m365-integration/package.json` | **absent** from `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `optionalDependencies` |
| declared by the root `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` | **absent** from both dependency fields |
| declared by **any** workspace member | **none** — `grep -rl '"@electric-sql/pglite"' --include=package.json services packages` returns nothing |
| where it resolves from | `Blockchain/Dev/node_modules/@electric-sql/pglite/dist/index.cjs` — hoisted to the workspace root, not under the service |
| why it is there | `npm ls`: `@secuura/originate` → `prisma@7.8.0` → `@prisma/dev@0.24.3` → `@electric-sql/pglite@0.4.1` (also via `pglite-socket@0.1.1` and `pglite-tools@0.3.1`, both deduped) |
| lockfile dependents | **3**, all transitive: `@prisma/dev` (`dependencies`), `pglite-socket` and `pglite-tools` (`peerDependencies`) |

**The two importers:**

* `services/m365-integration/src/__tests__/ks1677-oauth-state-statements-on-a-real-engine.test.ts`
* `services/m365-integration/src/__tests__/ks1673-teams-statements-on-a-real-engine.test.ts`

**Positive control that the measurement is live:** the same resolution check run for a declared dependency of this service resolves under the expected path, and the m365 suite itself ran **23 files / 220 cells / 220 passed / 0 failed** on this clone — so the two files above really do import successfully today.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

The hazard is not hypothetical for this exact subtree. **KS-664 records that a lockfile regeneration already moved it**: that ticket's description notes the regen *"downgraded …* `@prisma/get-platform` *7.8.0→7.2.0"* and **dropped** other packages outright. A dependency this service's tests rely on is therefore sitting one unrelated lockfile operation away from disappearing, and the failure mode is a **load failure** — which reds a whole file with no useful message and can poison a denominator rather than producing one honest red cell.

## Suggested fix

Declare `@electric-sql/pglite` in `services/m365-integration/package.json` `devDependencies` at the version already resolved (`0.4.1`), so the dependency the tests actually use is stated by the package that uses it. `services/originate` already depends on Prisma for its own reasons; nothing there needs to change. Worth checking whether other services import it undeclared too — not measured here.

## Board search

Over the whole corpus — **1682 issues, archived included, pagination exhausted, measured 2026-10-20T01:09:59Z** — exact substring over title + description:

* `pglite` → **1**, KS-664, which mentions it only inside a list of versions a lockfile regeneration moved. KS-664 is the deepmerge-ts advisory override; it does not mention `m365` (checked: false) and does not mention an undeclared dependency (checked: false). **Not a duplicate.**
* `electric-sql` → 0 · `undeclared dependency` → 0 · `transitive dependency` → 0
* `@prisma/dev` → 4 (KS-1290, KS-530, KS-493, KS-470), all about advisories or lockfile discriminators, none about this

**Positive controls, same corpus and moment:** `m365-integration` → **35**, `package.json` → **80**, `hoisted` → **25**. The instrument reports matches when there are any.

## How it was found

Gate BW1 on PR #1660 raised it as pre-existing residue, framed as "not declared in m365-integration's package". Re-measured by Seat R 59th rather than relayed, which sharpened it: **nothing** declares it, not just this service, and the real parent is another service's Prisma. Nothing built here.

nodes.title: Refs KS-1682: the three fail-closed warnings go through the service logger, and gate BW1's two notes

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Facts from QA gate 189 (PR 2001, KS-1256) that answer this ticket's open question: a second service imports `@electric-sql/pglite` without declaring it, the api-gateway real-engine test. Added by the close-out seat; nothing here changes the ticket.

- The file: Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1256-settings-store-statements-on-a-real-engine.test.ts, line 15, imports the package. This seat re-read it at origin/develop 035685291b9d: Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/package.json has 0 hits for pglite (control: 2 hits for vitest in the same file), and Blockchain/Dev/package.json has 0.
- Gate 189 measured this (source: /Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-04_gate189-ks1256-pr2001/verdict.md, G189-F5, line 44). In the lock the package comes only from the dependency tree of the prisma dev package. With a workspace-scoped install (--workspace=services/api-gateway --workspace=packages/shared), 2 test files fail: the import itself, plus 1 new TS2307 in KS-1090's type-check baseline. A full root npm ci passes 154 of 154 files and 1623 of 1623 tests. The gateway Dockerfile build excludes src/__tests__, so images are unaffected.
- So what this ticket calls latent is already a failure for a scoped install in api-gateway. The fix shape is the same as here, declare it in the package that imports it. This note does not choose it.
- Not measured by this note: any other service (this ticket's question still stands beyond m365-integration and api-gateway); a run of either install.

State corrected: In Review to Todo. Nothing is under review on this ticket.

Done: the measurement only; the ticket's own text says "Nothing built here". The linked PR 1662 is merged but belongs to KS-1682 (the fail-closed warnings through the service logger) and does not touch this defect. No commit on develop at b1fb543640e7 names KS-1694, and no package.json there declares `@electric-sql/pglite` (git grep, with a control hit on prisma in originate).

Left: the suggested fix is not applied. `services/m365-integration` still does not declare the dependency (the ticket suggests a devDependencies entry at 0.4.1). The ticket also leaves open whether other services import it undeclared.
